subject: dwarfBlacksmith
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.

spec.name: Dwarf Blacksmith at the Anvil
spec.description: A stout Warcraft-style dwarf smith in horned steel helm, blue tunic, leather apron and big braided ginger beard, one fist raising a runed smithing hammer and the other gripping tongs that hold a glowing bar on an anvil atop a log stump.
spec.layout: Stylized Blizzard/Warcraft proportions: the dwarf is about 1.5 m with the helm, and the pitch is chunky: a head about 1/4 of the body height, a barrel chest, shoulders wider than the hips, huge pauldrons, thick tree-trunk legs, oversized boots, and fists as big as the face's lower half. He stands centred on x = 0 at z about 0 and faces +Z, leaning a touch forward. The stump stands in front of him at z 0.4..1.0 with the anvil on it (long axis along x, horn pointing to the model's left, +X, face top at y 0.78). The dwarf's right hand (-X) holds a smithing hammer cocked up above the anvil's rear half; his left hand (+X) holds long tongs gripping the end of a glowing orange bar lying on the anvil face. The beard hangs in front of the chest as a big silhouette from chin to belt, built from a solid core plus broad overlapping braid blades and gold rings, in root-to-tip tones (dark red root, ginger body, pale gold tips). Warcraft look on every part: bold faceted low-poly forms, painterly hue-shifted tones (warm tones on top, cooler and darker below), steel and leather with gold trim and rivets, rim-lit blue runes, and hot-metal glow. Soot and wear are separate small pieces: dark smudges on the apron and knuckles, scuffs on the anvil face. The lowest points are the boots (y = 0) and the stump base (y = 0). The tallest point is the helm horns (about 1.65). The hammer head tops out at about 1.45. Nothing sits in front of the face except the beard's mustache, below the nose.

parts.builds: Both stumpy legs from hip to floor. Thick trousers in 'trousers' (smooth swept tubes bending at the knee) with leather knee guards in 'leather' with 'gold' rivets; steel greaves with 'steelDark' edging and 'steelLight' highlight strips down the shin; heavy cuffed boots (chunky box and wedge soles in 'leatherDark', uppers in 'leather', broad steel toe caps in 'steel' with rivets, 'leatherLight' lace strips and buckle straps with 'gold' buckles, thick sole edge in 'ink'); small soot smudges at the toes; the lower hem of the pelvis and the crotch gusset in 'trousers'. Both legs are mirrored pairs and are slightly splayed outward in a stable stance. Rides hipL..toeL and hipR..toeR (and hips for the pelvis block).
parts.attaches: Top of the legs meets the torso at the hipsRoot mount and the belt at y about 0.66; the boots stand on floorFeetL and floorFeetR (y = 0, lowest points sink at most 2 cm). The apron from the torso hangs in front of the thighs at z above 0.2, so keep the thigh fronts at z <= 0.2.

parts.builds: The barrel body from belt to collar, y 0.3 to 1.22. A wide rounded loft torso in 'tunic' (a Warcraft-blue tunic: big chest, round belly) with 'gold' trim bands at hem and collar, lacing strip on the chest. A wide 'leather' belt (swept loop round the waist) with a big 'gold' buckle carrying an anvil-and-hammer emblem built from small parts in 'goldDark', 'ink' and 'steelLight', plus belt pouches, a hammer loop and 'steel' studs at beltFront. A long 'leather' smith's apron: front panel from chest to knee (y 0.3) with a bib, 'leatherDark' stitched border, cross-straps over the shoulders and behind the neck, a pocket with 'steel' rivets, 'ink' soot smudges and scorch marks, and a small hanging 'leatherLight' tool roll. Huge pauldrons on both shoulders, centred on the shoulderL and shoulderR mounts: layered curved 'steel' plates (3 stacked lathes or wedges per side) with 'gold' rims, 'steelLight' edge highlights, rivet rows and one big upward spike on each, one 'runeBlue' glow rune on each. A gorget collar in 'steel' with 'gold' trim at the neck, a leather backpack or bedroll with straps on the back (z down to -0.28), and a small 'runeBlue' glow rune medallion on the chest strap. Rides hips, spine, chest.
parts.attaches: Bottom meets the legs at y about 0.66 and at hipsRoot; the apron hangs over the thighs down to y 0.3 and stays at z <= 0.26. The neck and collar meet the head at neckBase. Arms start under the pauldrons at shoulderL and shoulderR (upper arms emerge at x about +-0.34, leave a clean opening). The beard from the head part falls in front of the chest at z above 0.26 down to y 0.82; keep the chest front, bib and any chest emblems at z <= 0.26 and do not put anything bigger on the bib above y 0.85.

parts.builds: The big characterful head, helm and beard. Head about 0.34 wide and 0.3 tall, a rounded block of 'skin' with a heavy brow ridge, wide cheekbones, a big bulbous nose in 'skin' with 'skinShade' underside and a pinkish 'skinShade' flush, a separate upper head and lower jaw (jaw joint) with a closed mouth line in 'ink', small round ears in 'skin' with 'skinShade' inner ear. Large eyes that read from the front: 'ink' outline, 'eyeWhite', 'iris' blue iris with 'ink' pupil and a tiny 'eyeWhite' highlight, under bushy overhanging brows made of 3 to 4 broad blades each in 'beardDark', 'beard' and 'beardHi'. A horned steel half-helm: 'steel' skull cap with 'steelDark' brow band and bolt rivets in 'gold', a 'gold' centre crest strip, 'steelLight' edge highlights, two big curved 'steelLight' to 'steel' horns (swept tubes, tips pointing up and out to y about 1.65), and cheek flaps over the ears; a nose-guard is NOT built, the face stays open. A huge ginger beard: a solid core silhouette from the cheeks to the belt (down to y 0.82, front at z about 0.38), plus a modest number of broad overlapping braid blades and 2 thick side braids with 'gold' rings and 'goldDark' beads, root-to-tip in 'beardDark' then 'beard' then 'beardHi'; a bold curling mustache with two braided tips below the nose, sideburns, and a small tuft of hair under the helm at the back. Everything in front of the face stays clear; the mustache sits below the nose. Rides neck, head, jaw.
parts.attaches: Neck sits at the neckBase mount inside the gorget collar. The beard front hangs over the chest and ends at y 0.82 and must not poke through the torso (the torso front is at z about 0.26). Helm top is at helmTop. The head must not collide with the hammer head at hammerHead (x -0.42..-0.14, y 1.28..1.42, z 0.5..0.62, in front of the face).

parts.builds: Both muscular arms and the tools. Bare 'skin' upper arms (chunky swept tubes, bulging biceps) coming from under the pauldrons and bending at the elbows, wrapped forearms with 'leather' bracers (bands in 'leatherDark', 'gold' rivets and laces) and 'skinShade' soot smudges and a few pale scars, thick 'leatherLight' gauntlet gloves with 'leatherDark' knuckle stitching, chunky fists with separate fingers and a thumb (digit joints). The dwarf's right hand (-X, at gripR) grips a big smithing hammer: 'wood' handle (swept, slightly tapered) with 'leatherDark' grip wrap bands and a 'gold' pommel cap, rising from the fist at about 80 degrees from horizontal to the head at hammerHead; the head is a heavy block (axis along x, about 0.28 long and 0.11 tall) in 'steel' with a 'steelDark' flat striking face, a 'steelLight' bevel, 'gold' collar bands and four 'runeBlue' glow rune marks on its sides. His left hand (+X, at gripL) holds long iron tongs: two 'steelDark' arm rods crossing at a 'gold' rivet at about [0.2, 0.84, 0.62], 'leatherDark' grip sleeves at the handles, flat jaws gripping the bar end at workpieceEnd (the tongs end exactly at that mount). Left arm mirrors right except bend pose. Rides shoulderL..fingersL and shoulderR..fingersR.
parts.attaches: Shoulders at shoulderL and shoulderR (under the torso's pauldrons). Left tong jaws at workpieceEnd on the glowing bar from the anvil part. The hammer head floats above the rear half of the anvil (z about 0.56, y above 1.28, x from -0.42 to -0.14), clear of the head part's face and helm.

parts.builds: The workstation under the smith's hands, built to the dwarf's footprint and simpler than him. A fat log stump (roughly a 12-sided prism, radius about 0.3, centred at x 0, z 0.71, y 0 to 0.4) in 'wood' with a 'woodDark' bark skirt, a 'woodDark' root flare at the base, a top disc with 'woodLight' style growth rings made of 'leatherLight' thin lathe rings and a 'woodDark' split crack, two 'steelDark' iron hoop bands with 'gold' rivets, chop scars; the stump top is at stumpTop (y 0.4). The anvil on top in 'anvilIron': a waisted body, a tall base foot with 'steelDark' ledges, a flat 'steel' face plate on top at anvilTop (y 0.78, about 0.45 long in x with a 0.2 square-ish face and a 0.15 chamfered rear), a pointed horn curling toward +X (the model's left) that reaches x about 0.6, a stepped heel and tail on the -X side with hardy hole and pritchel hole in 'ink', 'steelLight' highlight edges, 'ink' soot and a few 'goldDark' scuffs, and a small 'runeBlue' glow rune on the front waist. Lying on the anvil face: a glowing hot iron bar (about 0.4 long along +x from workpieceEnd, 0.035 square) in 'ember' with a 'hotYellow' hot tip end and 'hotYellow' core strip; plus 6 to 8 tiny 'hotYellow' and 'ember' spark chips hovering above the bar and 2 or 3 small 'ink' scale flakes on the face. Nothing else is staged around them. Rides the root joint hips only as a rigid prop (a static prop, no extra joints).
parts.attaches: Stands on the floor at y = 0, the stump centred at x 0, z 0.71. The bar starts at workpieceEnd [0.12, 0.805, 0.72], where the tongs from the arms part hold it, and lies on the anvilTop face at y 0.78. The hammer from the arms part is cocked above and behind the bar and does not touch it.

calls.reasoning:
I'm designing the spec for a stylized Warcraft-style dwarf blacksmith at an anvil, working out proportions—chunky stature around 1.4m tall with broad shoulders—and planning the scene elements like the anvil, hammer, and a glowing workpiece.

I'm breaking the figure into parts: lower body with boots and apron, torso with pauldrons, head with beard and helmet, arms holding hammer and tongs, plus the anvil, stump, and sparks. I'm also pinning down joint positions, starting with the hip root and overall height including the helmet.

For pose, I'm going with a relaxed working stance rather than a T-pose — arms bent forward with the right hand resting the hammer on the anvil face and the left holding tongs gripping a glowing bar, keeping shoulder, elbow, wrist, and basic hand joints.

Now I'm working out the anvil geometry: centered at z=0.72 with the top surface at y=0.80, sitting on a 0.45-tall stump, with its long axis running along x and the horn pointing toward +X since the dwarf stands facing it from the side.

I'm sizing up the overall figure's bounding box, deciding the dwarf's back-to-front depth, total width including pauldrons and the anvil horn, and settling on roughly 1.4 width by 1.75 height before moving to the joint rig names.

Setting up the skeleton joints...

Toe joint continues the leg chain with a forward direction and leg role. Now I'm placing the arms: shoulderL angled forward-down toward the chest, with elbow and wrist positions sized to match upper arm and forearm lengths, aiming the left hand toward the anvil area since it holds tongs.

I'm leaning toward an asymmetric pose for liveliness, but keeping it close to symmetric and neutral for rigging: the left arm lowered toward the anvil, the right arm raised with elbow bent so the hand can hold the hammer upward near the anvil's working height. I'm placing the right shoulder, elbow, and wrist to form this raised forearm, with the hammer extending upward from the hand.

Working out the hammer's tilt and position above the anvil, and setting overall figure height around 1.7 to account for the helmet horns reaching toward 1.62. I'm also sketching finger joints for each hand (thumb and a simplified finger chain) and placing tongs in the left hand gripping a glowing bar that rests across the anvil's surface.

I'm defining ownership between parts: the arms own the hammer and tongs, while the anvil part owns the workpiece bar, with a shared mount point marking where the tongs' jaws grip the bar's end near the anvil face.

Adjusting positions so the hammer head sits just above and slightly behind the anvil's left half, cocked back in position; the anvil itself is sized oversized for a stylized dwarf-forge look, around 1.1 units wide with the stump and body stacked to a face height near 0.86.

I should recenter the anvil at x=0 with the horn pointing +X, adjusting its box to roughly -0.5 to 0.6, which simplifies the asymmetry concern. I'm placing the anvil top mount point so it sits near the dwarf's chest height relative to his belt and overall body proportions.

Defining the legs/boots part with its bounding box and joints, covering greaves, metal toe caps, straps, and trousers, while deciding the leather apron should belong to the torso part and extend down to overlap the legs.

Now I'm figuring out torso's bounding box to accommodate the apron's overlap with the legs box, keeping them separated by depth rather than height so parts meeting at a boundary still share faces cleanly. I'm listing torso contents: pelvis/belt, chest tunic, apron, pauldrons, gorget, straps, belt buckle emblem, and tool loops, and sizing its box accordingly.

For the head, I'm including the skull, nose, eyes, brows, ears, horned helm, braided beard with rings, mustache, hair, and jaw, giving it a tall bounding box since the dwarf's beard drapes down past the chin to chest height. I'm resolving the overlap between the beard and torso by pulling the torso's front depth in slightly so the beard can drape over the chest without colliding, adjusting both boxes' z-ranges to stay just clear of each other.

Next I'm defining the arms group — shoulders, bracers, gloves, hands, hammer, and tongs — with a wide box since the pauldrons belong to the torso and the arms start just below the shoulder joints; I'm considering rolled-up sleeves with bare, fur-covered forearms, leather bracers, gauntlets, and a rune-etched smith's hammer. Then for the anvil setup I'm laying out the tree stump base with growth rings and axe marks, the anvil itself with horn, hardy hole, face, metal bands, and a rune emblem, plus a glowing metal bar and scattered ground debris, while deciding whether to add a small hammer or quench bucket resting against the stump.

Now I'm checking which parts touch the floor — legs, stump, and anvil base — and tallying up a part budget: roughly 150 for legs, 200 for torso, 220 for head, 200 for arms, and 130 for the anvil, totaling 900. I'm also settling on a saturated, chunky Warcraft-style palette with ruddy skin tones, fiery ginger beard shades, blue eyes, steel and gold armor accents, and warm leather browns.

Still defining color palette...

That's too many colors for the palette limit, so I need to trim down to around 24, consolidating things like skin highlights and pupils into shared outline/ink tones to stay within budget.

Finalizing the palette at 24 colors, trimming trousers and tunicDark while adding beardDark and an ember highlight tone. Now I'm moving to defining the mount points, starting with the hammer grip position.

Working out the hand grip coordinates relative to the wrist, then placing mounts for the neck base, helm top, beard root, shoulders, and pauldrons so the torso and arm pieces attach correctly.

I'm deciding the arms have bare upper-arm skin under the pauldron, leather bracers on the forearms, and gauntleted hands, then defining the war hammer's geometry -- setting the handle axis and head position relative to the gripped hand.

Next I'm placing the tongs in the left fist, laying out the two crossing arms meeting at a rivet point, and positioning the jaws so they grip the end of a bar that extends outward along the x-axis.

I'm now checking the arm joint coordinates for both sides — shoulders, elbows, wrists — and making sure torso width, hip width, and pauldron radius all line up consistently against the anvil and hammer proportions.

I'm also figuring out overall bounding box size, roughly [1.2, 1.7, 1.3], and deciding the torso's back edge should start around z=-0.28, skipping extras like a backpack or cape for simplicity. Now I'm moving on to positioning the head joint and skull center.

For the head, I'm sizing it large and dwarf-proportioned, with a wide braided beard hanging down the chin dyed in gold rings, bushy brows, a prominent nose, and a horned open steel half-helm with a brow band so nothing obstructs the face. Once the head geometry and horn height are settled, I'll move on to writing out the full spec text with the layout and joint list.

Now I'm working through the skeleton: defining joint parents and roles down each leg (hip, knee, ankle, toe) and arm (shoulder, elbow, wrist, fingers/thumb) with left/right symmetry, then assigning direction vectors for spine, neck, head, jaw, and limbs based on their approximate positions so each bone points toward its child joint.

Writing final JSON...

I'm writing buildLegsBoots and need to type its context parameter, but Ctx is supposed to come from the module, so I'm weighing whether to import it or sidestep the issue with a local type or an inline `any` destructure.

Still writing the thigh and shin geometry...
